answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism in an agent economy is capital-bonded identity proofs. Each new agent must lock a minimum stake of value tokens along a shared verification ridge. Only after peers confirm genuine activity does the system release a small nectar reward, and any failed challenge echoes back as a slash. Attackers who spawn many identities must post the full stake for every fake account, so the total capital cost scales linearly with the number of sybils and quickly exceeds any reasonable budget.
